posts.title: Introducing Firn: A Self-Hosted Endurance Training Heatmap

posts.title: Grant Docker Access To Volume on SELinux Enforced System
posts.description: Note Docker can do everything this post describes automatically, you just need to set either the :z or :Z option on your volume. ( Docker Documentation ) When running Docker on a system enforcing SELinux, Docker Volumes require a special SELinux context to be accessible by the Docker Daemon and Container. This context is called container_file_t and can be set on a path recursively : semanage fcont
